verdict.rationale: First-party docs establish modular building blocks: declarative components with scoped CSS, plus .svelte.js/.ts modules for reusable reactive logic and state shared across the app. The dependency-injection half rests only on one community report praising Svelte's Context system for sharing state, with no first-party documentation of an injection mechanism. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the context/dependency-injection API (setting and getting injected dependencies through the component tree), concrete examples of injecting services into components.

support.subject: As a developer, I can organize my app into modular, dependency-injected building blocks

citations.quote: This is useful for creating reusable reactive logic, or sharing reactive state across your app
CSS inside a <style> block will be scoped to that component.
Svelte Stores and the Context system are great for sharing state
